title: Configured short interval writes report before planning
query: A project automation calls interval-update for a short review window and next-window plan, with context_refs asking for the latest report from a longer planning interval. What should it load, write, and avoid?
reference_points: Loads default goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, and PM thread refs
Resolves the configured latest longer-interval report as parent context when present and labels it as a source gap when missing
Writes a date-stamped .farplane/reports/interval/<interval_id>/<timestamp>.md report before durable goals or ticket mutation
Plans only the configured planning_window
Does not select due jobs, update scheduler state, or perform broad strategy replanning

title: Configured interval gates material goals deltas
query: An interval review wants to change the north star after reading configured interval_output_refs from another interval inside the review window. What gates apply?
reference_points: Loads farplane/goals.md plus the configured interval_output_refs inside the review window
Labels missing or stale evidence as source gaps
Writes the interval report before mutating farplane/goals.md
Requires approval for north-star, KPI, strategy-axis, quarterly, yearly, or durable milestone changes
Routes executable changes into tickets or Goal Advisor handoffs

title: Interval context refs stay additive
query: A project automation calls interval-update with project_root, interval_id, windows, one extra customer-doc ref, and codex_attention_drift enabled. What should the automation include, and what should the skill resolve itself?
reference_points: Automation passes project_root, interval_id, review_window, planning_window, additive context_refs, and report_workflows only
interval-update resolves default goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, PM manifest, and report roots
context_refs may add parent context, interval outputs, extra refs, or true replacements
report_workflows controls optional workflows such as codex_attention_drift instead of the skill assuming daily or weekly behavior
The automation should not restate every default Farplane path or gate
Project-specific profiles stay in automation prompts or project docs, not generic skill first-load refs

title: Interval reports are date-stamped
query: A configured interval run succeeds. Where should the report go and how should consumers find the newest one?
reference_points: Writes a date-stamped report under .farplane/reports/interval/<interval_id>/
Does not use latest.md as the canonical report
Consumers find the newest report by timestamp sorting or explicit links in subsequent reports
No tracked config or scheduler state is mutated just to store last_report
